notes.title: Frebbventure Alliance - Playable alpha demo!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=5GlZ8_Qg8fg;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Suffering from post-Frebbventure depression? It's been known to happen, but now you needn't suffer anymore! [u][b][url=https://almyriganhero.itch.io/frebbventure-alliance]Go on, give it a look![/url][/b][/u] [/h2]

What's new? What's different? Nothing, but also everything. It's the exact same formula you loved the first time, but faster, smoother, prettier... good music-ier, and even more jam packed than last time. More enemies, more bosses, more level variety, more platforming mechanics, and more playable characters with more customization.

The biggest changes to the formula are that you now control a tag team of two characters at the same time (DKC style, there's no weird gimmicks or shoddy follower AI getting in the way,) and that the the bonus objective system has been replaced with slightly more standard collectable crystals and a style/ranking system based on avoiding damage and chaining together currency pickups and enemy KOs. 

(Don't worry if you get a C rank or lower on your first passthrough; it's meant to be a VERY strict system. Even I can barely get an S rank on most levels!)

notes.title: Sequel in the Works
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=mZjb0haxMK4;full][/previewyoutube]


Amongst at least half a dozen prototypes for "my next big game" and beside a relative side-project or two Erma, a viable Frebbventure sequel is finally starting to take shape! "Frebbventure Alliance" is the working title. What's different this time around?

Nothing but also everything. It's still a fast-paced, combat-focused action platformer with Kirby-style movesets. It's still heavy on story and especially atmosphere, and it's still playable at a base level with a nearly unlimited technical skill ceiling. There are, however, still a few major changes, beyond better level design and moveset flow and crisper art.

First and most obviously, the tagteam character system. Wasn't it neat, being able to bring one of four completely unique characters with their own moves and gimmicks into any level you wanted? Well now you can bring TWO with you, and the overall tally isn't finalized, but there'll be a GOOD DEAL more than 4 total, this time around!

Second is the points and ranking system. If you're a sucker for score attacks and S-rank hunts, this simple addition will crank the game's intensity dial from 11 to 22. Not only does almost every action aware points and almost every mistake subtract them, but a time bonus along with multiple combo and streak systems will do their best to keep you on edge the whole time.


This is obviously still very early-days, but for anyone who might be interested but isn't keeping up with me off of Steam itself, I figured I may as well at least bring it up. If you do wanna follow and possibly support development (though discussion and eventually playing demos, not financially. ...For now.) then you can check out my server here: https://discord.gg/kmrhFHT8XK

notes.title: Savegame format change
notes.content:
I've finally got around to replacing the old encrypted save system with something that should allow you to transfer save files more easily. This new file format will automatically copy, [b]but not replace,[/b] the data from your old files upon booting the game. If you navigate to the "Frebbventure" folder in AppData/local, you might see for example a file named

"frebbventure_save1.sav"

along with one named

"frebb_save_1_newformat."

In case the name doesn't make it obvious enough, the latter is your new, transferable save file. I should note, this is purely a futureproofing feature: if your old file has ALREADY been separated from its original machine, this process will, sadly, not recover it. You'll need to remove it from the folder, or the game will still crash at the file select screen.

Once your new format file has been generated, feel free to remove your old files (but, just in case this all goes belly-up, you should probably back them up.) I plan to eventually introduce cloud saves, and you won't want your outdated saves transferring between machines.

notes.title: The 'Rox Your World' patch
notes.content:
The point of this latest patch is to make Roxy a more fun character to play as based on user feedback, [b]and absolutely not to fix yet another handful of crashes.[/b]

[b][u]The main changes to her are:[/u][/b]

- She now starts moving a BIT faster from a standstill.

- Overall air control is more sensitive.

- Her dodge covers significantly more ground. It's still nowhere near as good as Drinn's, but it's not quite borderline useless anymore.

- Her aerial up attack has a slightly larger hitbox, and gives a stronger upward boost.

- Her shoulder slam has received the most adjustment. It now grants more initial speed (especially when used midair,) but can also be slowed down faster by holding the opposite direction. Speaking of midair use, it now functions as a VERY weak double-jump, but can also be cancelled into her up-air at any time. While it has always been cancellable into a belly slam for precision landing, this new option is useful in far more cases.


She is still by design "the powerful fat combat character," but hopefully these changes will make her a BIT less painful to use in tricky platforming sections.

notes.title: Next patch delayed because I bricked my PC trying to upgrade RAM
notes.content:
Disclaimer: DON'T PANIC! I already backed up the most recent development build. It is stored safely, soundly, and snuggly across multiple redundant devices.

That being said, while attempting to install a pair of 8GB ram sticks early this afternoon, I may or may not have completely and utterly destroyed the only (relatively) powerful and up-to-date machine in my household. Best case scenario, I get it into a professional place next Monday, and they have it fixed by Tuesday, after which I can continue bug squashing. Likely case: I'll have to buy a new computer, probably a renewed or refurbished one, on the cheap. It could be more than a week before I get it, it might not be functional, and I might have to return it and wait another week or so to get another one.




If you reach the true final boss, more specifically the true true final phase, which is an autoscrolling SHMUP (spoiler,) wait out the sweeping eye laser attack and deal the last couple blows a second or two after it disappears. If it dies while the laser is out, the game will crash. No I don't know how neither me nor my testers caught this, but credit to StarvingHound for being the one to find it.

notes.title: Feedback Patch 1 complete
notes.content:
[h1]Remember the good old days when games worked out of the box?[/h1] [b]I don't, I grew up with the GameCube, and if Sonic got absorbed by a solid stone wall and fell into the void, that was YOUR problem. Hallelujah to the digital age![/b]

A bit less than a week in, and already a ton more bugs have been found and patched (you don't want to read all of them... I don't want to admit all of them... ːsteamsadː ) but that's not all! Here're some neat little quality of life changes made at the behest of helpful players:


[b]- All characters (except Drinn) now start with 1 extra heart of HP -[/b]
Because this game, and its bosses in particular, can be hard. Harder than I set out to make it, honestly. It's tough, balancing a game around the experience of yourself and a small group of dedicated testers. The game performed decently at previous SAGE outings, but indepth feedback was in fairly short supply.

...Drinn is already OP enough as is though, so no buffs for her.


[b]- Camera has been significantly improved -[/b]

Now instead of constantly wheeling around to try and GUESS where you want to go and how fast you're trying to get there, the camera is just shifted more to the right of the screen. There're a few spots in the game where this could be slightly less convenient, but given all those bugs I don't want to admit I had to patch, I've decided to save theory crafting the most elegant possible solution for Feedback Patch 2.

You can also now hold the UP or DOWN key while standing still to take a quick peak up or down. I tried my best to eliminate spots where this would even be needed during the level design phase, but it was requested by a friend of a friend, and adding it didn't hurt.


[b]- Subtle red screen flash on player hurt -[/b]
Just because a couple people mentioned not always noticing when they've taken damage.


[b]- Hitting lava (and its counterparts) now cancels ground pounds and fast fall -[/b]
This is one I've been meaning to change for a while, but just never got around to. Previously, hazards like lava and acid that bounce you upwards on contact wouldn't reset your gravity, meaning it was possible to get caught in an inescapable damage loop when using certain abilities.


[b]- Frebb's midair handling has been tamed -[/b]
Finally found the line in my spaghetti code that made the main character turn so fast midair! His weight now feels far more natural midair, and precision platforming should be much easier.


[b]- F12 now takes screenshots -[/b]
Didn't even know I had to do this manually, and never thought to test it because I quite frankly forgot screenshotting with F12 in Steam games was a thing it's been so long since I used it.
